questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/afc9e81f3294803794ba0d62773958913cf7475a0718e77052212a149050aecf.png)

Consider the segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ above, and the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2u+2v-2,\,y=v-u+2.
$$

The image of $\overset{―}{PQ}$ under the action of $T$ is the segment $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}$ in the $xy$-plane. Which of the following diagrams shows $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u+2v-2 \\ v-u+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u+2v \\ -u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the endpoints of $\overset{―}{PQ}$ to the endpoints of $\overset{―}{{P}^{′}{Q}^{′}}.$ So, to find the image of $\overset{―}{PQ},$ we find the images of each endpoint.

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing the endpoints of our segment:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 10 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 8 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the endpoints of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-6,2)$ and $(8,1).$

Drawing this segment in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/8e57b4d47ef3c6ad1b1d70a97126aa865c4481ee67e16eaf4e79c09e3146b30d.png)

questions.problem:
Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2u-v,\,y=u+3v-1.
$$

Let $P(2,-2)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ u+3v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ u+3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(6,-5).$

x=Au+b,

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3v+u \\ u-6v+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+3v \\ u-6v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$

$$

$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(7,-17).$

Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=v-2u-3,\,y=u+v+3.
$$

Let $P(1,1)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$

An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-2u-3 \\ u+v+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2u+v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Polygon Under an Affine Transformation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/838861910879e95b0e1c3055da9f9597f194950c3823867a20a1e3c149354437.png)

Consider the rectangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=2u-v+1,\,y=u-v+1.
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v+1 \\ u-v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/c89be48140d49ce8c9def44122aa2bfac779bdd02cfbfbe98f97d414a5637409.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(1,1),(3,2),(1,0),$ and $(-1,-1).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/d038caec0aa360e5d8cc1bcb4a3aa4d88408496d947b312d47634e51bbf4a11f.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/9bfb4e21205db9550d88222e04449b9858137550b957ba652b3e6998dce8025c.png)

Consider the triangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,-1\le v\le 1,\,0\le u\le \frac{1-v}{2}}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/194428bede19351ba77866a9ca49f76b38c4327fd0a5e2c219afff9c14b12c28.png)

             

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our triangle:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-2,0),(-1,-1),$ and $(0,2).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/02ab748669496bf50a8809cf822a969d731a18283d52272175fd5b615ef5b765.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=2>0,$ this transformation preserves orientation.

\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ u-v-1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/06ceacb05656e99e545561e5cd5733529a1cf7f052beb6086b2fd42667041713.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-1,-2),(1,0),(2,-1),$ and $(0,-3).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/92b9079151925202a5346e6b1dd2082b21a4e4102720673773e958c5f3644c4f.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-2<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.

questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=-2v+1,\,y=4u-v-5.
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=-4$
- The transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is false. Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2v+1 \\ 4u-v-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2v \\ 4u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].$

- Statement II is false. Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}|=0\cdot (-1)-4\cdot (-2)=8.
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, since $det(A)>0,$ the affine transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Area Scale Factor of an Affine Transformation
questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=0\cdot 2-1\cdot 4=-4.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|-4|=4.
$$

$$

$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+7 \\ u+v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $\mathbf T$ maps the endpoints of $\overline{PQ}$ to the endpoints of $\overline{P'Q'}.$ So, to find the image of $\overline{PQ},$ we find the images of each endpoint.

- The matrix $U$ containing the endpoints of our segment:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/faf8bd29c9813cf0f73fca4b58f5636d3eb3262eae64ac099bdcdc569096ab0c.png)

$$

An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3u+4 \\ 4v-2u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3u \\ -2u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $\mathbf T$ is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/8c90983944994c315715ff8545d3cffd5e791c23e8ad035bdc3b4c810659442e.png)

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/a9a49eaf4203133b1c47ab30b75fde67af56172ae6c4e59d12a2f7e9df3d46c1.png)

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|\det(A)| = |12| =12.
$$
